question: A 29-year-old woman presents to the clinic regularly with her young daughter and complains that ever since her last delivery 5 years ago, she has been having intermittent light vaginal bleeding. She has seen several doctors so far and even some ‘specialist doctors.’ Her menstrual history also appears to be variable. Physical examination is within normal limits. Her urine analysis always seems to have > 10 RBCs/hpf. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.opa: Munchausen disorder with a primary gain
options.opb: Malingering disorder with a secondary gain
options.opc: Factitious disorder with a primary gain
options.opd: Factitious disorder with a secondary gain
